claims.text: Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering above 2300 °C.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 typically has relatively large grains.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 typically contains residual porosity.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 has limited mechanical integrity during prolonged exposure to corrosive liquids.
A liquid-phase precursor route such as molten-salt or sol-gel synthesis can produce nanoscale ZrB2 powder.
Liquid-phase-precursor-derived ZrB2 can be densified and formed as a single phase at approximately 1800–2000 °C.
The proposed processing route generates a transient liquid during sintering.
The transient liquid promotes particle rearrangement.
The transient liquid enhances diffusion during processing.
Enhanced particle rearrangement and diffusion permit ZrB2 densification at a lower temperature.
The proposed route produces nanoscale or significantly refined ZrB2 grains.
The proposed route minimizes residual porosity and creates a more uniform microstructure.
A fine, low-porosity ZrB2 microstructure provides greater mechanical strength and integrity.
Reduced porosity leaves fewer pathways for ingress of the corrosive plating-bath liquid.
Compared with conventionally prepared ZrB2, liquid-phase-processed ZrB2 will resist hole formation more effectively during long-term plating-bath exposure.
Compared with conventionally prepared ZrB2, liquid-phase-processed ZrB2 will have a lower failure rate during long-term plating-bath exposure.
The plating-bath service environment may impose thermal cycling and corrosive attack.
The approach is intended to remain applicable only if processing retains single-phase ZrB2 without deleterious secondary phases.
